text:
leo: Quick question — how are we treating 'shrinkwrap'/lockfile dependency fixes vs behavioural bug fixes for semver? e.g., we had a tiny yarn.lock update that changed CI hashes. Should that trigger a patch bump, or can we avoid bumping product version and just publish an internal maintenance tag?

maya: If the change is strictly lockfile/transitive pin with zero code change -> prefer no public semver bump. We can publish an internal release artifact, but avoid incrementing product version unless customer-facing behaviour changed.

anita: I'm leaning the other way — bump patch for anything we ship. Patch bumps are low cost and keep changelog linear. Otherwise we end up with mismatched build metadata.

sasha: Reminder: our deploy-bot only watches tags that match `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. If we start using ad-hoc suffixes like `-locks` or `-ci` deploy-bot will ignore them unless we change the pipeline. That will complicate rollouts.

leo: Concrete example: current tag is `v1.8.12`. We update yarn.lock only. Options: publish `v1.8.12+locks`, `v1.8.13`, or a non-semver annotated release. Which is least friction?

maya: I'd avoid metadata suffix for prod. `v1.8.13` patch is simplest for ops and changelog automation. Mark the release body: "maintenance: lockfile only."

anita: Semver purists will object: patch implies a bug fix in product code; lockfile updates don't change our public API so semver is semantically wrong.

sasha: Operational compromise: create `v1.8.13` but annotate with `maintenance` label. Update changelog generator to add `[maintenance]` when present. That keeps tooling working.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Starting rollout for tag `v1.8.13` to prod-us-central — stage 1/3.

leo: Also want rule for reverts: if we revert a behavioural change (rollback of code) -> patch. If we revert a config-only or doc change -> no bump.

maya: Proposal draft: 1) user-visible bug fixes -> patch. 2) API/contract changes -> minor. 3) lockfile / build metadata / CI-only changes -> no semver bump, but create annotated internal release OR 4) if it's a security-related pin -> patch and include CVE note.

anita: Concern: our changelog tooling aggregates tags to build release notes. If we skip tags it will skip entries. That hurts audits.

sasha: Implementation idea: release script accepts `--maintenance` which still creates a `vX.Y.Z` tag but sets a `maintenance: true` field in the GitHub release body and adds `[maintenance]` prefix in changelog. That preserves semantics for tooling and keeps deploy-bot happy.

leo: :thumbsup: that feels pragmatic. Can we enforce security pins always bump patch and get backports?

anita: yes — security pins are mandatory patch and backport to supported branches (stable/maintenance branches).

sasha: I'll add a guard in the release pipeline: if PR is labeled `security` then require semver patch increment and add `security` tag in release notes.

leo: I'll write a short RFC and include the `--maintenance` flag spec + changelog examples. For now team consensus: create semver patch tags for lock/security changes (but mark maintenance in release body) and avoid bumping for pure doc/README/ci script tweaks. Posting RFC before EOD.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Rollout succeeded for tag `v1.8.13` — 5/5 nodes healthy.
